audience.text: Python developers building 3D content pipelines, especially in 3D printing, CAD, and visualization workflows requiring OBJ, STL, glTF, COLLADA, and 3MF support.

capabilities.text: Read OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, COLLADA, and 3MF files using Scene.open() with automatic format detection or explicit FileFormat specification.
capabilities.title: Load multiple 3D formats

capabilities.text: Write scenes to OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, and 3MF using Scene.save() with format-specific SaveOptions for compression, coordinate flipping, and unit scaling.
capabilities.title: Export to common 3D formats

capabilities.text: Construct hierarchical scenes using Node.create_child_node(), access child_nodes, and manipulate independent Transform properties per node.
capabilities.title: Build and traverse scene graphs

capabilities.text: Create meshes via Mesh.control_points and Mesh.create_polygon(), or convert primitives using to_mesh() and PolygonModifier.triangulate().
capabilities.title: Construct and edit mesh geometry

capabilities.text: Attach LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, or PbrMaterial to nodes and configure diffuse, specular, albedo, metallic, and roughness properties.
capabilities.title: Assign materials to nodes

capabilities.text: Build animation clips using AnimationClip, AnimationNode, and KeyframeSequence, and store skeletal bind-pose data with Pose and related types.
capabilities.title: Support keyframe animation

limitations.text: FBX export is not implemented; FbxExporter.save() and save_to_stream() raise NotImplementedError.
COLLADA export is not reachable through Scene.save() due to exporter lookup order issues.
Scene.render() and the entire aspose.threed.render module raise NotImplementedError.
Texture and TextureBase raise NotImplementedError on construction; image-backed textures cannot be created.
Mesh boolean operations (union, difference, intersect) raise NotImplementedError.
NURBS curve evaluation and surface-to-mesh conversion raise NotImplementedError.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic 3D scene manipulation in Python without requiring native SDKs or external binaries.
Supports conversion between common 3D formats including OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, COLLADA, and 3MF through a unified Scene API.
Provides parameterized primitives and direct mesh construction for building custom 3D geometry from scratch.

product_summary.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for Python is a pure-Python, MIT-licensed library for loading, constructing, and exporting 3D scenes without native dependencies.

uncertainties: The exact set of supported 3D formats beyond those explicitly listed in format facts is unclear.
Whether FBX import works reliably with real-world files is uncertain given only tokenizer tests exist.
The behavior of Scene.save() when no format is detectable from a stream without filename is unclear.
The scope of 'experimental' for FBX support beyond export not being implemented is not detailed.
Whether all listed public symbols are fully functional or partially stubbed is not verified by examples.
The compatibility of the library with Python versions beyond 3.7–3.12 is not confirmed.
The availability of documentation links beyond those in the README is not verified.
The exact test coverage for triangulation and polygon operations is not quantified beyond file counts.

workflows.name: Import and inspect a 3D model
workflows.text: Load a 3D file using Scene.open() and traverse its node hierarchy to inspect geometry and structure.

workflows.name: Export a scene to glTF
workflows.text: Build a scene with primitives or meshes, assign materials, and save to glTF format using GltfSaveOptions.

workflows.name: Export a scene to STL
workflows.text: Construct a mesh from control points, attach it to a node, and export to ASCII STL using FileFormat-based save options.

workflows.name: Export a scene to 3MF
workflows.text: Build a cube mesh programmatically, assign it to a node, and save to 3MF using ThreeMfSaveOptions with compression control.

workflows.name: Convert primitives to editable meshes
workflows.text: Instantiate parameterized primitives like Box or Sphere and convert them to Mesh objects via to_mesh() for further editing.
